title: CI check: validate model metadata schema diffs + generate release note preview artifact
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelog/release notes
description:
Context
- We’re standardizing model/version metadata (schema v1) and generating customer-visible release notes automatically. Today reviewers can merge metadata changes without seeing (a) what the public release note would say or (b) whether a change accidentally leaks internal-only fields.
- This ticket adds required CI checks so every model metadata change produces a deterministic “release note preview” artifact and fails fast on schema/redaction violations.

Goals
1) Prevent invalid schema diffs from merging (schema v1 + invariants).
2) Produce a human-reviewable release note preview from the same pipeline/templates used by Console + docs.
3) Enforce public vs internal field separation (redaction rules) at review time.
4) Provide stable artifacts that Support/Release Eng can reference when debugging “missing/incomplete release notes”.

Non-goals (explicit)
- Full customer notification subscriptions (email/webhook) and downstream comms.
- Backfilling historical release note pages beyond minimal smoke coverage.

Implementation plan
A) Add a CI workflow (GitHub Actions) that runs on PRs touching:
- model registry records (metadata payloads)
- schema definition files (JSON Schema / protobuf-style spec)
- release note templates/category mapping

B) CI steps
1. Detect changes
   - Determine whether the PR includes any of:
     * /schemas/model-metadata/v1/**
     * /models/** (registry records / fixtures)
     * /changelog/** (templates/category mapping)
   - If none: job should noop quickly.

2. Schema validation (hard fail)
   - Validate all changed metadata JSON documents against schema v1.
   - Validate “invariants” beyond JSON Schema (implemented as a small validator script):
     * semantic version string format for model versions and variant versions
     * required compatibility constraints present when runtime/tokenizer requirements change
     * deprecation fields must include timeline + replacement pointer
     * public_text must be present for any customer-facing category event

3. Schema diff / breaking-change guard (hard fail)
   - When schema files change, compute a diff summary for review:
     * Added/removed required fields
     * Changes to enums
     * Changes to constraints (regex/min/max)
   - Fail if:
     * a required field is removed/renamed without an approved migration flag
     * a public field is moved to internal-only (or vice versa) without explicit justification string
     * schema version number not bumped when required-field set changes
   - Note: this is a “policy check”, not a full OpenAPI-style breaking change analyzer.

4. Release note preview generation (required artifact)
   - Run the changelog generator in “PR preview mode” against the diff:
     * input: git diff (base..head) of model metadata + change events
     * output: generated release note entry/entries
   - Emit two artifacts:
     1) public_preview.md (what customers would see)
     2) internal_preview.md (includes internal-only fields + audit pointers)
   - Include a machine-readable artifact for downstream tools:
     * preview.jsonl (one entry per generated note, stable keys)

5. Redaction enforcement (hard fail)
   - For public_preview.md + preview.jsonl, ensure:
     * internal-only fields never render
     * “reason”/“incident link”/“account name” patterns are blocked
     * any “quality metric” claims require a referenced eval_run_id + significance flag when present
   - For internal_preview.md, allow internal-only but still enforce “no secrets” policy (tokens/keys/credentials).

6. Reviewer UX
   - Post a PR comment with:
     * summary (categories/severity, affected models)
     * direct links to artifact downloads
     * any failures, with actionable remediation steps

C) Required checks / merge gating
- Make the CI job required for the redwood-model-registry repo (initially).
- Roll out to other repos that touch templates / generator once stable.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Any PR touching model metadata or schema must run the job.
- [x] Invalid metadata fails with a clear error pointing to file/field.
- [x] Any schema “breaking” change fails unless an explicit migration/override is present.
- [x] A release note preview is generated and uploaded as an artifact on every relevant PR.
- [x] Public preview cannot contain internal-only fields; failures block merge.
- [x] PR comment includes links to artifacts + a summary that matches generated content.
- [x] Job completes in <= 6 minutes for typical PRs (<= 30 changed model records).

Testing plan
- Unit tests for diff classifier + redaction rules.
- E2E tests using fixture PRs:
  1) metadata-only change (non-breaking, perf note)
  2) schema change adding optional field
  3) schema change removing/renaming required field (should fail)
  4) attempted inclusion of internal_note in public_preview (should fail)

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: false positives on “breaking change” detection.
  Mitigation: start with conservative rules; add an override label (“release-notes-approved”) gated to release engineers only.
- Risk: artifact contains sensitive content.
  Mitigation: public preview redaction + internal preview secret scanning; keep artifact retention short (7 days) by default.

Links
- GitHub PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr-18452-add-ci-check-release-note-preview-on-metadata-diff.json
- Related tickets: ENG-9821 (schema v1), ENG-9823 (generator API), ENG-9825 (redaction rules)
- Release process thread: sources/gmail/connor_obrien/20251007-release-train-add-release-note-preview-check.json

Rollout notes
- Phase 1 (this ticket): required check in model registry repo.
- Phase 2: propagate workflow to redwood-docs + control plane repo (where templates/events are authored).
- Phase 3: enforce “no silent promotions” by requiring a generated note for any promotion event (separate policy ticket).
comments: 2025-09-30 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted CI workflow outline. Plan is to run on PRs that touch /models or /schemas, otherwise noop. Added note to include both public/internal preview artifacts so support can debug discrepancies.

2025-10-02 (Connor O'Brien): Please make the check required before we start the migration backfill PRs. Also, we need a PR comment with a one-paragraph summary; reviewers won’t click artifacts unless prompted. Suggest retention 7 days for artifacts.

2025-10-03 (Marcus Lin): Security note: internal preview artifacts are still considered sensitive; ensure they do not include account names, incident URLs, or anything from private Slack threads. Add secret scanning before upload (even for internal).

2025-10-06 (Quentin Harris): Breaking-change guardrails: schema required-field removal should hard fail unless schema version bump + migration flag present. Also enforce that any new public field has a style-guide-compliant description string.

2025-10-08 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented diff summary and redaction enforcement. Added an override label restricted to Release Eng org team per Connor’s suggestion; override still logs a warning in the PR comment.

2025-10-11 (Chloe Martin): Please ensure the preview generation uses the same templating library as the generator service (no duplicated logic in CI). Otherwise Console vs CI will drift and we’ll lose trust in the previews.

2025-10-14 (Sahana Iyer): Merged workflow changes behind a feature flag, then enabled required check for the repo. Typical runtime 3m40s on fixture PR, 5m10s worst-case on 30-file change. Artifacts upload verified.

2025-10-17 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done. Required check enabled; release train comms sent. Follow-up: create a short reviewer guide in Confluence on how to interpret the preview output and when to request editorial review.
